caption: Datasets and benchmarks that the surveyed studies use to train and test their detectors, in order of the year each was introduced
note: Note: a dash (—) means that the review's extraction records give no value for that property, not that the dataset lacks it. Text without a citation draws on the study named in the "Introduced by" column; a citation anywhere else in a row points to a different study.

rows.scale: 720K training images, 18,000 fake and 18,000 real in each of 20 ProGAN categories [C15]; 11 per-generator test sets
rows.generators: Training: ProGAN; 11 test sets: BigGAN, CRN, CycleGAN, DeepFakes, GauGAN, IMLE, ProGAN, SAN, SITD (StyleGAN2 tested separately), StarGAN, StyleGAN
rows.notes: GAN-era protocol: ProGAN for training, unseen generators for testing. Standard training set in later work [C15, C16, C22]; several more detectors train on ProGAN, using 1, 2 or 4 of the 20 categories [C21, C39, C40], 200K of its images [C43] or all 20 categories [C48]. The authors' "for now" caveat: future generators may escape detection

rows.scale: 720K ProGAN images for training; 19 test subsets [C41, C48]
rows.generators: BigGAN, CRN, CycleGAN, DALL-E, DeepFakes, GauGAN, Glide, Guided, IMLE, LDM, ProGAN, SAN, SITD, StarGAN, StyleGAN
rows.notes: Adds diffusion and autoregressive subsets to the test side of the ForenSynths protocol; the 19 subsets have since become the standard test suite for CLIP-feature detectors [C41, C48]

rows.generators: 8 diffusion models: ADM, DDPM, iDDPM, LDM, PNDM, SD-v1, SD-v2, VQ-Diffusion
rows.notes: Published together with the DIRE detector; covers diffusion-generated images only

rows.scale: More than 1M fake and 1,331,167 real images
rows.generators: 8 generators: ADM, BigGAN, GLIDE, Midjourney, SD v1.4, SD v1.5, VQDM, Wukong
rows.notes: Sets out two explicit tasks: cross-generator and degraded-image classification. Its authors report that detection drops sharply across generators and for low-resolution, JPEG-compressed and blurred inputs. Later shown to carry biases in JPEG compression and image size [C31]

rows.scale: 2,496,738 images in total (964,989 real and 1,531,749 fake)
rows.generators: 13 GANs, 7 diffusion and 5 other methods (25 in all)
rows.notes: Aimed at robustness; the authors' own detector was scored on the IEEE VIP Cup 2022 test sets. The authors note that state-of-the-art detectors still have difficulty with generators absent from training

rows.real_source: Not applicable: AI-generated images and their metadata, collected from Twitter
rows.notes: Gathered from a platform, not generated for research; included at screening as evidence of synthetic images already circulating in the wild

rows.scale: 60,000 real and 60,000 synthetic images, 120,000 in total
rows.generators: Stable Diffusion v1.4, a latent diffusion model
rows.notes: One generator only, at a 32×32 resolution; the authors' Grad-CAM analysis shows background imperfections driving the classification
Large set of diffusion images, published at ECCV 2024 alongside a contrastive detection method; included at screening as a secondary study, hence no full-text extraction row

A benchmark of realistic in-the-wild images. AIDE, the detector proposed in the same study, averages 92.77% accuracy on AIGCDetectBenchmark and 86.88% on GenImage but reaches only 65.77% on Chameleon; the authors describe the problem as far from solved

rows.generators: 4,803 generators, covering GANs, commercial models and both latent and pixel diffusion
rows.notes: Made to check whether diversity of generators leads to generalisation. Its authors note that diffusion models are over-represented in the dataset and that error rates are still too high for critical uses
Hierarchically organised set of AI-generated images; a secondary study included for this table alone, hence no full-text extraction row
